title: Docs Site: SDK sample rotation and issue synthesis playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes the end-to-end process for maintaining a curated matrix of SDK examples (the "Sample Catalog"), rotating and retiring samples regularly, and creating an issue-synthesis pipeline that turns recurring support incidents and telemetry signals into updated, canonical example code and docs edits. The goal is to keep examples accurate, minimal, secure, and aligned with runtime and API changes while reducing support toil.

Scope: Applies to all SDK sample code and small reference applications hosted in the docs site and the SDK repositories (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java). It covers: authoring standards, review cadence, automated validation, rotation schedule, mapping to product priorities, and the remediation path for support-derived fixes.

Owner and stakeholders
- Document owner: Engineering Developer Experience (DevX) team (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Primary stakeholders: SDK teams (Python/JS/Go/Java), Runtime product, DX Docs, Support & Customer Success
- Secondary stakeholders: Security, Observability, Solutions Engineering

Goals and success metrics
- Accuracy: 0 known example regressions in production-facing docs for 30 days after release.
- Freshness: rotate at least 30% of the Sample Catalog each quarter for major API surface changes.
- Support reduction: 25% fewer "example bug" tickets year-over-year attributed to our documented samples.
- CI health: All sample validation jobs green before docs publish.

High-level lifecycle (concise)
1) Catalog: maintain a living YAML/JSON manifest (sample-catalog.yaml) listing each sample, SDK language, primary intent, owner, last-updated, stability tag (stable/experimental/retired).
2) Validation: run language-specific linters, unit smoke tests, runtime contract tests, and snippet extraction validation on every PR.
3) Rotation: scheduled quarterly review + on-demand churn for breaking platform changes.
4) Issue synthesis: automated aggregation of support tickets, telemetry alerts, and crash logs mapped to catalog entries; create remediation work items and track via the "sample-fixes" board.
5) Release: publish updates with release notes and tagging; notify downstream repos and customers as needed.

Authoring standards (applies to all samples)
- Small is better: prefer 10–30 lines for inline page snippets. Full examples may be larger but should live in the samples repo.
- Copy/paste-safe: no production secrets, no hard-coded tenant IDs. Use environment variables and small bootstrap instructions.
- Deterministic outputs: where possible, use fixed seeds or deterministic model prompts in examples, and show sample input/output in comments only.
- Minimal dependencies: prefer only official SDKs and widely adopted libs; document required versions.
- Multi-language parity: every canonical sample must have parity mappings for supported SDK languages where feasible.
- Licensing: include license header in sample repo files matching Redwood standard (Apache-2.0).

Snippet extraction and docs pipeline
- Snippet format: use the standard snippet markers used by the docs site generator: // BEGIN_SNIPPET <id> and // END_SNIPPET <id> (or block-style for markdown fenced snippets).
- Extraction CI: incremental snippet extraction on PRs produces a "snippet diff" that is validated against the sample-catalog manifest (ensures snippet id, language, and page mapping exist).
- Validation steps (CI):
  1. Lint (language specific)
  2. Build/Install deps (isolated env)
  3. Smoke run (execute main path or unit test)
  4. Output assertions (for deterministic snippets)
  5. Size check (inline snippets < 200 lines)
- Failure handling: failing jobs should add a descriptive artifact to the PR with stdout/stderr, failing test file, and suggested remedial steps.

Sample Catalog (manifest) - example YAML schema (as a single-line table for docs)
- Path: /repos/docs/samples/sample-catalog.yaml
- Required fields per entry: id, title, language(s), page, owner, stability, last_updated, test_job_id

Example manifest table (rendered as text table)
| id | title | languages | page | owner | stability | last_updated |
| sample.chat.basic | Basic chat loop | python,ts | /docs/sdk/chat | eng-dx | stable | 2027-01-10 |
| sample.embed.search | Embeddings search | python,ts,go | /docs/sdk/embeddings | eng-dx | experimental | 2026-09-08 |

Rotation cadence and criteria
- Quarterly scheduled pass (default): review samples with last_updated > 90 days and stability=experimental first.
- Triggered rotation (on-demand): API contract changes, runtime behavior shifts, security advisories, or when a support cluster shows >5 related tickets in 14 days.
- Retirement criteria: low usage (<5 page hits/month), unmaintainable dependency, or duplicated capability covered by newer sample. Retired samples move to a /retired folder and maintain an archive entry in the catalog.

Automated issue synthesis pipeline (implementation summary)
- Inputs: support ticket labels (example-bug, sample-mismatch), stack traces, telemetry alerts (snippet failures, example runtime exceptions), periodic fuzz tests against samples.
- Mapping: use a deterministic mapping table that correlates error signatures to sample IDs. When a match probability > 80% we auto-create a remediation ticket in the sample-fixes board; when 30–80% we create a flagged suggestion for a human reviewer.
- Ticket template fields: sample_id, observed_symptom, telemetry_links, reproducer-snippet, priority (P1–P4), owner, proposed-fix-surface (docs, sample code, CI).
- Escalation: P1 or high volume items are auto-notified to the SDK owner, Support TL, and DevX lead.

Release checklist for sample updates
1) Update sample file and manifest entry.
2) Ensure CI validation green across all languages listed.
3) Update page with snippet ids; run docs-site preview tests.
4) Bump sample-catalog.yaml last_updated and add short changelog in manifest.
5) Create release PR with the tag "sample-release" and link runtime/product change if applicable.
6) Post release note in #devx-docs Slack and the monthly sample digest channel.

Rollback and emergency hotfix process
- If a sample update breaks CI or causes incorrect guidance in the docs, create a hotfix branch named hotfix/sample/<sample-id>/<short-reason>.
- Revert path for docs-site: revert the snippet PR, re-run snippet extraction, and republish docs via the emergency docs pipeline (see docs-site emergency-patch playbook).
- For customer-impacting sample regressions (support escalations pointing to production code failures), fast-track a patch release and coordinate with Support and Customer Success for guidance and mitigations.

Top support issue categories and canonical fixes (examples)
1) Example fails due to auth change (most common): Fix = update sample to use new header format, add a pre-run check that validates token env var and provide helpful error text.
2) Dependency breaking change: Fix = pin supported dependency version in sample manifest and add a compatibility note.
3) Runtime mismatch (generation parameters changed): Fix = update snippet default params and add comment block that explains tradeoffs for latency vs cost.
4) Multi-language parity gap: Fix = add a minimal TS/Go mapping and mark as "work-in-progress" in manifest.

Canonical fix template (to include in remediation PR)
- Problem statement (1–2 lines)
- Root cause analysis (2–4 lines) with links to telemetry or ticket ids
- Change summary (what changed in sample or docs)
- Validation steps (how we validated)
- Rollout plan (tags, publish, notify)

Observability signals for sample health
- Docs page hits (pageviews per sample page)
- Snippet CI pass rate (percent of PRs with snippet validation passing)
- CR (customer reports) rate with label example-bug/sample- mismatch
- Execution failure rate from fuzz tests and nightly sample runs
- Time-to-fix for sample-related tickets

Roles & Responsibilities (concise)
- DevX (owner): sample catalog, snippet CI, coordination with SDK owners, run quarterly reviews.
- SDK owners: update language parity, validate runtime compatibility, respond to P1/P2 sample fixes.
- Support: apply labels and sanity-check mapping when filing tickets.
- Docs engineering: snippet extraction tooling, preview pipeline, and emergency publish path.

Quickstart: adding a new canonical sample (step-by-step)
1) Create sample in /repos/docs/samples/<language>/<sample-id>/ with README.md and tests.
2) Add entry to sample-catalog.yaml with required metadata.
3) Add snippet markers and reference IDs in the target docs page.
4) Open PR to samples repo and docs repo simultaneously (link PRs).
5) Wait for CI: fix lint/build/test failures.
6) Request review from SDK owner and DevX reviewer.
7) Merge after approvals; CI will publish preview and then the live page in the next docs deployment window.

Example API snippet (Python)
# BEGIN_SNIPPET sample.chat.basic.py
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-medium', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Say hello'}])
print(resp.text)
# END_SNIPPET sample.chat.basic.py

CI snippet validation command examples
- python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
- pytest tests/test_sample_chat.py -q
- node ./scripts/verify-snippets.js --manifest sample-catalog.yaml

Governance and cadence summary
- Quarterly review, weekly automated issue-synthesis runs, and on-demand emergency patches.
- Triage meeting cadence: DevX + Support weekly sync for high-volume sample issues.
- Quarterly business review: report sample freshness, support reduction, and top 10 remediations.

Appendix: small checklist for reviewers
- Does the snippet run in an isolated environment?
- Are secrets or production values absent?
- Is the sample consistent across languages? If not, is there an explicit note?
- Does the manifest entry include an owner and test_job_id?
- Are there telemetry/alerts tracking this sample?
